title: Texas's 4th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 4th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Pat Fallon against Democratic nominee Jason Pearce. The district, which stretches from Dallas-Fort Worth exurbs to the Oklahoma and Arkansas borders, underwent a contentious mid-decade redistricting in 2025 that was ultimately upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court. With a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+16 and a 'Solid R' rating from the Cook Political Report, the district is considered heavily Republican, and Fallon is favored to win a fourth term. Key issues include cost of living, healthcare affordability, national security, and the fallout from the 2025 redistricting fight.
polling_note: No district-specific public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. Only generic Texas-wide congressional ballot polls exist, which are not applicable to this specific district.

candidates.name: Pat Fallon
candidates.summary: Pat Fallon is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2020. A Republican, he chairs the House Armed Services Subcommittee on Military Personnel and serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Accountability. Prior to Congress, Fallon served in the Texas House (2013-2019) and Texas Senate (2019-2021), and was a Frisco city councilmember and mayor pro tem.

candidates.name: Jason Pearce
candidates.summary: Jason Pearce is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 4th Congressional District, having won a competitive primary in March 2026. A Plano native, Pearce worked in sales, mortgage lending, and insurance before leaving his job to campaign full-time. His campaign focuses on lowering the cost of living, affordable healthcare, fair wages, worker protections, corporate accountability, and clean government.
